_note: Module 7 chat scenarios (synthetic-authored). facts: what the simulated user knows; given: facts already in the opening message; needed: facts a diagnosis needs.

sessions.title: AV1 stutter
sessions.opening: Our AV1 trailer stutters on some of our test phones. What's going on?

facts.decoders: MediaCodecList only shows c2.android.av1.decoder for AV1, rated up to 1920x1080 at 30 fps.

sessions.cause: The phone has no hardware AV1 decoder; the software decoder c2.android.av1.decoder tops out at 1080p30, so 4K60 cannot keep up.
sessions.next: Serve a 1080p30 AV1 or an HEVC rendition to devices whose AV1 decoder is software only.

sessions.title: AV1 stutter (all details)
sessions.opening: A 3840x2160 60 fps AV1 clip stutters on a phone whose only AV1 decoder is c2.android.av1.decoder (software, max 1080p30). Why?
sessions.cause: The only AV1 decoder is a software one rated for 1080p30, far below the clip's 4K60.
sessions.next: Pick a lower AV1 rendition or HEVC for devices without a hardware AV1 decoder.

sessions.title: Slow MP4 start
sessions.opening: Our progressive MP4s take ages to start playing over the network.

facts.layout: ffprobe lists the top-level boxes as ftyp, mdat, moov.

sessions.cause: The moov box sits after mdat, so the player must download the whole file before it can start.
sessions.next: Remux with the moov box at the front (ffmpeg -movflags +faststart).

sessions.title: Slow MP4 start (all details)
sessions.opening: Progressive MP4s start slowly over the network; the top-level boxes are ftyp, mdat, moov. Why?
sessions.cause: moov comes after mdat, so playback waits for the end of the file.
sessions.next: Remux with -movflags +faststart so moov comes first.

sessions.title: Lip sync
sessions.opening: Lip sync is off in one of our clips. Can you help?

facts.offset: ffprobe says the video stream starts at 0.300 s and the audio at 0.000 s.

sessions.cause: The video stream starts 300 ms after the audio, and the player does not compensate for the start-time offset.
sessions.next: Honour the stream start times (or re-mux with aligned timestamps) and retest sync.

sessions.title: Washed-out HDR
sessions.opening: HDR videos look washed out on one of our phones.

facts.display: Display.getHdrCapabilities() returns no supported HDR types on that phone.

sessions.cause: The display does not support HDR, and the HDR10 video is shown without tone mapping to SDR.
sessions.next: Detect missing HDR support and tone-map to SDR (or serve an SDR rendition).

sessions.title: Thumbnail crash
sessions.opening: Our thumbnail generator crashes after a while. Any idea?

facts.log: Logcat shows 'Failed to allocate codec: insufficient resources' after the fourth decoder.
facts.code: We create a new MediaCodec for each thumbnail and never call release().

sessions.cause: Decoders are never released, so the app exhausts the device's codec instances.
sessions.next: Call release() on each MediaCodec (or reuse one decoder) and cap concurrent decoders.

sessions.title: Thumbnail crash (all details)
sessions.opening: Thumbnail generation fails with 'insufficient resources' after a few clips; we never call release() on the decoders. Why?
sessions.cause: Unreleased decoders exhaust the limited codec instances.
sessions.next: Release each MediaCodec when the thumbnail is done.

sessions.title: Live resume
sessions.opening: Our live stream errors out when users come back to the app.

facts.log: The player throws BehindLiveWindowException on resume, after about two minutes in the background.

sessions.cause: After a long pause the playback position falls behind the live window, so the player throws BehindLiveWindowException.
sessions.next: Catch BehindLiveWindowException and re-prepare at the live edge.

sessions.title: Audio over calls
sessions.opening: Our app's audio keeps playing over phone calls.

facts.code: We start the player directly; we never request audio focus.

sessions.cause: The app never requests audio focus, so it is not told to pause when a call takes focus.
sessions.next: Request audio focus with AudioFocusRequest and pause on focus loss.

sessions.title: No HD with DRM
sessions.opening: Customers never get HD streams on DRM-protected content.

facts.level: MediaDrm reports securityLevel L3 on those phones.

sessions.cause: Widevine L3 devices only get SD keys under the license policy; HD keys need L1.
sessions.next: Check the security level and serve SD to L3 devices, or adjust the license policy.

sessions.title: No HD with DRM (all details)
sessions.opening: Phones that report Widevine L3 never get HD keys. Why?
sessions.cause: L3 is software-only, and HD keys are usually restricted to L1.
sessions.next: Serve SD to L3 devices or relax the policy for HD.

sessions.title: Main10 decode failure
sessions.opening: Some HDR clips fail to decode on one phone.

facts.decoders: The phone's HEVC decoder only lists the Main profile.

sessions.cause: The device's HEVC decoder supports Main but not Main10, so 10-bit clips fail.
sessions.next: Check profile support with CodecCapabilities and fall back to an 8-bit rendition.

sessions.title: Washed-out HDR (all details)
sessions.opening: HDR10 clips look washed out on a phone whose display reports no HDR support. Why?
sessions.cause: HDR10 is shown on an SDR display without tone mapping.
sessions.next: Tone-map to SDR or serve an SDR rendition.

sessions.title: Stripes in gradients
sessions.opening: Our gradient-heavy intro shows visible stripes after encoding.
sessions.cause: Banding: smooth gradients quantised at 8 bits and a low bitrate turn into visible steps.
sessions.next: Encode in 10 bit, add grain or dither, or raise the bitrate for the intro.

sessions.title: Blocky sports
sessions.opening: Fast scenes in our sports stream turn into blocks.
sessions.cause: The bitrate is far too low for 1080p60 motion, so the encoder quantises heavily and blocks appear.
sessions.next: Raise the bitrate for the 1080p60 rendition or lower the resolution and frame rate.
